name: Default suite `pytest:qa` exits 1 with 0 collected and no captured output — every whole-tree QA gate inherits a phantom `tests.run-error`
description:
QA-measured defect from shift 12 (2026-11-23T08:41Z). Found while gating the two `Review` cards; it is the reason every whole-tree `qa_review_changes` on this project returns `require_approval`.

## Measurement (reproducible)
| call | result |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:qa")` | `exited with code 1`, **0 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors / 0 skipped**, `seconds: 0.0`, one finding `[medium] tests.run-error` |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:qa", extra_args=["--collect-only","-q"])` | identical: `exited with code 1`, 0 collected, `seconds: 0.1` |
| `qa_plan()` | `default_suite: pytest:qa`, cwd `qa`; the other declared suite `npm` is reported unavailable (`npm` not in PATH) |
| `qa_review_changes(scope="all")` | `require_approval`, 12 findings, and the run line `pytest:qa: exited with code 1` |

This is a **VitePress documentation project**: `qa/` contains `README.md`, `security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md` and `tests/site-integrity.test.mts` — a vitest `.mts` suite, no Python test file anywhere in the project root. A `pytest` suite is the wrong default for this tree, and it fails before collecting anything.

## Why it matters
1. **It masks real signal.** Every whole-tree gate carries an `tests.run-error` medium finding, so a genuine `change.missing-tests` and a broken environment look the same in the verdict. The two Review cards this shift (`97583327`, `46c91d6b`) both carried it.
2. **It is unactionable by design.** `qa_run_tests` reports the exit code but **no captured stdout/stderr**, and the QA profile does not execute arbitrary commands, so neither I nor the card owner can see *why* it exits 1. Compare with the `EUSAGE` case in `qa/README.md:16-17`, where the lockfile error is quoted verbatim — the gate should do the same for a suite it declares itself.
3. Per the standing QA rule, "a suite that cannot run is a HIGH environment finding, not a pass" — but here it is worse than absent: an absent suite would be reported honestly.

## What to do (pick one, state which)
- **A (recommended, smallest):** stop declaring `pytest:qa` as the default for this docs project — repoint the default to the vitest suite (`npm test` in `docs/`) once `537e8ee7` makes it executable, and remove `pytest:qa` from the suite map. Coordinate with card `e684ce5c` which owns the `qa_policy` declaration write.
- **B:** if `pytest:qa` is meant to exist, make it discover something: identify its `cwd`/`paths`, add the missing config, and prove a real collection count.

Independently of A/B: **`qa_run_tests` must capture and return the command's stderr/stdout on a non-zero exit.** Without it, `tests.run-error` findings are unclosable.

## Acceptance criteria
- `qa_run_tests(suite="auto")` on this project either runs the vitest suite and reports real counters, or reports *only* `tests.no-suite` honestly — no `exit code 1` with 0 collected behind a medium finding.
- A deliberately broken suite command produces a verdict containing the actual error text (proves the output capture), not just the exit code.
- `qa_review_changes(scope="all")` no longer lists `tests.run-error` among its findings for an unrelated docs diff.

## Owner
`software_developer` (QA tooling: output capture, suite map). Read-only for the QA profile — I do not write the fix.

`software_developer` (QA tooling: output capture, suite map). Read-only for the QA profile — I do not write the fix.

**QA re-measurement, shift 15 (2026-11-24T17:5xZ) — the finding is unchanged, and one of its acceptance criteria needs a correction.**

Current state, measured this shift:

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| `qa_plan(scope="all")` | `suites_json: [{name: npm, available: **false**, reason: "npm not found in PATH"}, {name: pytest:qa, cwd: "qa", command: ["python3","-m","pytest"], available: **true**, reason: ""}]` · `default_suite: pytest:qa` |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:qa", timeout=300)` | `decision: require_approval`, **passed: false**, 0 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors / 0 skipped, **0.1 s**, one finding `[medium] tests.run-error @ -` — *"Inspect the command output and fix the environment, then re-run."*, no stdout/stderr |
| `read_folder("qa")` | `README.md`, `security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md`, `tests/site-integrity.test.mts` — **no `.py` file at all** |

Two things to fold into the fix:

1. **`available: true` is a lie with a cost.** The flag is a probe of the *binary*, not of *collection*: `pytest:qa` is advertised as runnable on a tree that provably cannot collect one test. That is worse than the `npm` entry, which is honest (`available: false` + `reason`). Acceptance addition: **`available: true` must imply "collected ≥ 1 test", or the entry must carry a `reason` like the npm one.** Otherwise every gate inherits the same medium `tests.run-error` and the medium tier becomes noise.
2. **Option A is now cheaper than it looked.** `package.json` `scripts.test` = `vitest run`, and `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts` falls inside vitest's default include, so nothing about the suite *declaration* needs writing — only the default pointer. But note the caveat from `b776e9a7`: the declared cwd is `qa` (project-relative) while the diff side is platform-root-relative, so simply repointing the default to `npm` will still map 0 tests (card `49007737` measured `test_files: 2, tests_selected: 0`). Repointing the default is necessary, not sufficient.

Unchanged and still the load-bearing half of this card: **`qa_run_tests` must return the command's captured stdout/stderr on a non-zero exit.** With 0.1 s and no output, an `exit code 1` is unactionable for both the owner and me.

Wake kept at 2026-11-25T08:40Z — no new wake needed; this is an evidence update, not a re-scope.
